readmeExcerpt:
# pstack Lauren Tan's [pstack](https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack) is an opinionated Cursor skill stack that improves agent outcomes. This is a port for Claude Code, Codex, Pi, GitHub Copilot and other agent harnesses. It tracks upstream and also carries named policy forks, each declared in [`tools/forks.json`](tools/forks.json). Tell `poteto-mode` your goal and it will invoke the correct workflow for the task. It keeps your code concise, simple and verified. For concurrency bugs and invariants that tests cannot reach, `/create-formal-verification-skill` picks the riskiest property in your code, verifies it with a tool that fits, and leaves a project skill the next agent reruns. The separate [agent-formal-verify](https://github.com/michael-denyer/agent-formal-verify) plugin goes deeper on the method, with guided TLA+ model checking, Lean proofs, and Kani for Rust. ## Install
Claude Code Run in Claude Code 2.1.292 or later: ```text /plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude /plugin install pstack@pstack-claude ```
Codex Run in your terminal: ```shell codex plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude ```
Pi Run in your terminal: ```shell pi install git:github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude ``` The package loads the skills and the pstack Pi extension, which adds the subagent, question, and wake-up tools the skills use, plus `/loop` and the routing instruction. Invoke a skill with `/skill:`.
GitHub Copilot Run in your terminal: ```shell copilot plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude copilot plugin install pstack@pstack-claude ``` This installs pstack for the Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot app, which share `~/.copilot`. Start a new session afterwards. Copilot ships no default pstack models, so the first skill that needs one runs `setup-pstack` to pick from the models your account lists, and later sessions reuse that choice. The Copilot build is tested on Copilot CLI 1.0.87 through 1.0.92. On those versions the routing hook's context reaches the session alongside other plugins' session-start context. If a later version keeps only one plugin's context, `setup-pstack` offers a [standing instruction](plugins/pstack/skills/setup-pstack/copilot.md#wire-it-in) for `~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md` instead. On 1.0.92, once the CLI caches its computer-use experiment assignment, `copilot -p` sessions list no plugin skills and a `skill` call returns "Skill not found". Interactive sessions, the hooks, and the agents are unaffected.
Other harnesses OpenCode (the CLI and the desktop app), Gemini CLI, Prime Agent, and skills-only Codex installs read skills from `~/.agents/skills/`. Run in your terminal: ```shell git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude cd pstack-claude mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills for s in plugins/pstack/skills/*/; do target=~/.agents/skills/"$(basename "$s")" test -e "$target" || test -L "$target" || ln -s "$(pwd)/$s" "$target" done ``` To update, run `git pull` in the clone, then run the `for` loop again to link skills added since the last run. These installs have no routing hook, so ask for `poteto-mode` by name or add a standing instruction to the harness's instruction file. See [shared installation](docs/reference.md#shared-skills-installation) for per-harness notes and uninstalling.
### Configure pstack routes tasks to `poteto-mode` automatically. At session start, a hook injects an instruction that points the agent at it: the plugin's hook on Claude Code, Codex, and GitHub Copilot, and the pstack extension on Pi. Codex runs the hook only after you trust it through `/hooks`. Other harnesses have no hook. Run `setup-pstack` to turn automatic routing on or off, change model defaults, or set a reasoning effort per role (`arena runners: opus @xhigh, fable @max`). ## Getting started ```text Use poteto-mode to fix the search filter resetting when I change pages. ``` For a bug, it reproduces the failure, uses `how` and `why` to investigate, delegates the fix, then reruns the failing case. If the fix crosses a function boundary, it brings in `architect` before implementation. You receive the fix and the failing and passing evidence. [Other playbooks](plugins/pstack/skills/poteto-mode/SKILL.md#playbooks) cover planning, features, refactoring, performance issues, investigations, prototypes, PR maintenance, shipping, and longer projects. ## Details - [Skills and slash commands](docs/reference.md#slash-commands) - [Runtime setup](docs/reference.md#runtime-support) - [Models and dependencies](docs/reference.md#configuration-and-dependencies) - [Maintenance and port scope](docs/reference.md#maintenance) ## Data handling pstack has no server or telemetry. Anything its skills ask your agent to read, including session transcripts, goes to your model provider. Scripts run locally, and PR tools use your GitHub CLI login. ## Contributing Thanks for helping make this port better. Bug reports, documentation fixes, and runtime improvements are welcome. See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md) for the checks and where your change belongs. Report vulnerabilities privately as described in [SECURITY.md](SECURITY.md). To support maintenance of this port, [buy the maintainer a coffee](https://buymeacoffee.com/codenyer). ## License This port, including its modifications and additions, is also [MIT-licensed](LICENSE), © 2026 Michael Denyer. Original pstack © 2026 Lauren Tan; imported cursor-team-kit and thermos skills © 2026 Cursor. See [LICENSE-cursor-team-kit](LICENSE-cursor-team-kit), [LICENSE-thermos](LICENSE-thermos), and [NOTICE.md](NOTICE.md).

releases.body:
An `@level` on a role now reaches the child as the dispatch's own effort field on every runtime: `effort` on the Claude Code `Agent` call, `reasoning_effort` on Codex's `spawn_agent` and Copilot's `task`, and `effort` on Pi's `agent` tool. The ten generated agents, `effort-<level>` and `poteto-agent-<level>`, are gone, and so is the `agents` list in the Claude Code plugin manifest. They existed only because the `Agent` call had no effort parameter, and Claude Code 2.1.292 added one. Without the list Claude Code registers the default `agents/` directory, so pstack's agent types are exactly the four under `agents/`: `comment-sicko`, `poteto-agent`, and the two thermo-nuclear subagents. The generator now fails if the manifest gains an `agents` list again. Claude Code 2.1.292 or later is required for `@level`.

On Pi, the `agent` tool takes an optional `effort` that the extension passes to the child as `--thinking`. A value outside the levels in `models.json` errors and names the valid ones, and no child starts. An agent file's `effort` frontmatter is no longer read, since no file under `agents/` set it. Omitting `effort` still runs the child at the parent's thinking level. @yehheng3-

`orch frontier set` no longer rejects every gh pull request row as invalid on gh before 2.80.0, whose `headRepository` carries only `id` and `name`. The gh query now asks for `headRepositoryOwner` too and builds the head repository from the owner's login and the repository name, as `watch-pr` already does, so it reads the same on every gh version. A malformed owner still fails the row, and a deleted fork still drops out of the chain. @newinh found and fixed it in [#288](https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude/pull/288).

On Pi, an agent's worktree is no longer removed as clean when `status.showUntrackedFiles=no` hides its new or ignored files from `git status`. The cleanup check sets `--untracked-files=normal` itself, as the worktree audit already did, and leaves the user's setting alone. The `/pstack-agents` read command now quotes a transcript path that contains spaces, quotes, `$`, or other shell syntax, so `tail -f` and `pi --export` get it as one argument. The `transcript:` line still shows the raw path. @EthanYoQ found and fixed both, in [#284](https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude/pull/284) and [#285](https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude/pull/285).
Build the Lever requires known-bad controls for each comparison output and refuses a match when required input is missing.

On Pi, a running agent's `list_agents` entry gains an `activity` field: its current tool call, or the last one once it ended, as the tool name and a one-line summary of its arguments, and the first line of its latest message. A footer line, `pstack: 2 running · a1b2c3d4 bash: ls -la`, names the count and the most recently active agent while any runs, including one `send_message` resumes after a reload, and clears when none does. The new `/pstack-agents` command shows each agent's status, activity, transcript path, and the command to read it: `tail -f` while it runs, `pi --export` once it ended. Activity is read from the child's RPC stream and held in memory. The extension never appends it to the session or sends it as a message, so the model sees it only in a `list_agents` result, and the child's session has no second writer. Only the top-level session sets the footer. @Nickonomic asked for a way to see a background agent's work while it runs (#279); this completes the live view that 0.9.89's transcript path began.

pstack

Lauren Tan's pstack is an opinionated Cursor skill stack that improves agent outcomes. This is a port for Claude Code, Codex, Pi, GitHub Copilot and other agent harnesses. It tracks upstream and also carries named policy forks, each declared in tools/forks.json.

Tell poteto-mode your goal and it will invoke the correct workflow for the task. It keeps your code concise, simple and verified.

For concurrency bugs and invariants that tests cannot reach, /create-formal-verification-skill picks the riskiest property in your code, verifies it with a tool that fits, and leaves a project skill the next agent reruns. The separate agent-formal-verify plugin goes deeper on the method, with guided TLA+ model checking, Lean proofs, and Kani for Rust.

Install

Claude Code

Run in Claude Code 2.1.292 or later:

/plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude
/plugin install pstack@pstack-claude

Codex

Run in your terminal:

codex plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude
codex plugin add pstack@pstack-claude
Pi

Run in your terminal:

pi install git:github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude

The package loads the skills and the pstack Pi extension, which adds the subagent, question, and wake-up tools the skills use, plus /loop and the routing instruction. Invoke a skill with /skill:<name>.

GitHub Copilot

Run in your terminal:

copilot plugin marketplace add michael-denyer/pstack-claude
copilot plugin install pstack@pstack-claude

This installs pstack for the Copilot CLI and the GitHub Copilot app, which share ~/.copilot. Start a new session afterwards. Copilot ships no default pstack models, so the first skill that needs one runs setup-pstack to pick from the models your account lists, and later sessions reuse that choice.

The Copilot build is tested on Copilot CLI 1.0.87 through 1.0.92. On those versions the routing hook's context reaches the session alongside other plugins' session-start context. If a later version keeps only one plugin's context, setup-pstack offers a standing instruction for ~/.copilot/copilot-instructions.md instead. On 1.0.92, once the CLI caches its computer-use experiment assignment, copilot -p sessions list no plugin skills and a skill call returns "Skill not found". Interactive sessions, the hooks, and the agents are unaffected.

Other harnesses

OpenCode (the CLI and the desktop app), Gemini CLI, Prime Agent, and skills-only Codex installs read skills from ~/.agents/skills/. Run in your terminal:

git clone https://github.com/michael-denyer/pstack-claude
cd pstack-claude
mkdir -p ~/.agents/skills
for s in plugins/pstack/skills/*/; do
  target=~/.agents/skills/"$(basename "$s")"
  test -e "$target" || test -L "$target" || ln -s "$(pwd)/$s" "$target"
done

To update, run git pull in the clone, then run the for loop again to link skills added since the last run. These installs have no routing hook, so ask for poteto-mode by name or add a standing instruction to the harness's instruction file. See shared installation for per-harness notes and uninstalling.

Configure

pstack routes tasks to poteto-mode automatically. At session start, a hook injects an instruction that points the agent at it: the plugin's hook on Claude Code, Codex, and GitHub Copilot, and the pstack extension on Pi. Codex runs the hook only after you trust it through /hooks. Other harnesses have no hook.

Run setup-pstack to turn automatic routing on or off, change model defaults, or set a reasoning effort per role (arena runners: opus @xhigh, fable @max).

Getting started

Use poteto-mode to fix the search filter resetting when I change pages.

For a bug, it reproduces the failure, uses how and why to investigate, delegates the fix, then reruns the failing case. If the fix crosses a function boundary, it brings in architect before implementation. You receive the fix and the failing and passing evidence.

Other playbooks cover planning, features, refactoring, performance issues, investigations, prototypes, PR maintenance, shipping, and longer projects.

Details

  • Skills and slash commands
  • Runtime setup
  • Models and dependencies
  • Maintenance and port scope

Data handling

pstack has no server or telemetry. Anything its skills ask your agent to read, including session transcripts, goes to your model provider. Scripts run locally, and PR tools use your GitHub CLI login.

Contributing

Thanks for helping make this port better. Bug reports, documentation fixes, and runtime improvements are welcome. See CONTRIBUTING.md for the checks and where your change belongs. Report vulnerabilities privately as described in SECURITY.md.

To support maintenance of this port, buy the maintainer a coffee.

License

This port, including its modifications and additions, is also MIT-licensed, © 2026 Michael Denyer. Original pstack © 2026 Lauren Tan; imported cursor-team-kit and thermos skills © 2026 Cursor. See LICENSE-cursor-team-kit, LICENSE-thermos, and NOTICE.md.

aiSummary.oneLiner: An opinionated agent skill stack for Claude Code and Codex to improve autonomous workflows.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Pstack is a specialized plugin and skill stack designed to enhance the capabilities of AI coding harnesses like Claude Code and Codex. It ports rigorous, verified agent workflows originally designed for Cursor into other terminal-based AI environments. The tool manages named policy forks to enforce concise, simple, and secure coding practices during autonomous generation. By invoking specific workflows based on user goals, it significantly improves the reliability and outcome of agent-driven development tasks.
keyFeatures: Workflow translation: Ports Cursor-specific agent primitives to work seamlessly with Claude Code and Codex.
Policy management: Maintains named policy forks to enforce strict coding standards and behaviors.
Goal-oriented execution: Automatically invokes the correct operational workflow based on the stated task goal.
Code verification: Integrates strategies to ensure AI-generated code remains concise, simple, and secure.
Multi-harness support: Designed to operate across various agent environments including Pi and OpenCode.

useCases.title: Autonomous code generation
useCases.description: Improve the quality and reliability of code generated by terminal-based AI agents.

useCases.title: Enforcing project standards
useCases.description: Use named policy forks to ensure AI agents adhere to specific repository formatting and architectural rules.

useCases.title: Complex refactoring
useCases.description: Guide agents through rigorous workflows to safely refactor large sections of a codebase.

useCases.title: Cross-platform agent tooling
useCases.description: Standardize agent behaviors across different AI harnesses like Claude Code and Codex.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: This project is for developers and prompt engineers who actively use terminal-based AI coding assistants and want to enforce stricter, more reliable workflows. It requires familiarity with CLI agent tools.
